newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia hopeful on CEFTA agricultural accord.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia hopeful on CEFTA agricultural accord.

text.p: Slovenia said on Friday it aimed to reach an agreement on liberalising trade in agricultural products with members countries of the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) by mid-September.

"We will continue our negotiations and hope to reach a result by the September meeting of Prime Ministers of the CEFTA countries," Marjan Senjur, Slovenia's Minister of Economic Relations and Development, told a news conference.

The conference followed a closed meeting of CEFTA economic ministers in the Slovenian tourist resort of Bled. Cefta currently comprises Slovenia, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Poland and Romania.
Prime Ministers of all CEFTA countries will meet in Slovenia's coastal town of Portoroz on September 12.
Senjur said Slovenia would be ready to liberalise agricultural trade only by 2001. Most other CEFTA countries believe liberalisation should be implemented in 1999.
Slovenia took over the CEFTA presidency in January after it joined the union in 1996.
